In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure and evolution of molecular gas in the interstellar medium.
the effects of magnetic fields on the structure and kinematics of turbulent molecular clouds.
understanding how turbulence and magnetic fields affect the structure and evolution of molecular clouds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the structure and dynamics of turbulent molecular clouds is a complicated function of the cloud's magnetic field strength and the initial conditions.
the structure and dynamics of magnetized turbulent gas clouds is complex and difficult to characterize.
the magnetic field is important for GMC structure, but not as important as turbulence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the density and velocity structure in our model clouds is qualitatively similar to that of real clouds.
the turbulent velocity and magnetic field structures are similar in the magnetically sub- and supercritical clouds.

the structure of turbulent molecular clouds is determined by a complex interplay between gravity and magnetic fields, and the resulting density, velocity, magnetic field, and polarization structure is difficult to interpret in terms of simple analytic models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
turbulence in magnetized molecular clouds is a highly nonlinear process that cannot be described by linear theory or a single parameter such as the Mach number.
the density and velocity structure of magnetically supercritical clouds is very similar to that of subcritical clouds.
the density, velocity, magnetic field, and structure of molecular clouds are strongly affected by turbulence.
